meta.title: Households (Demo)
meta.description: A WordPress app for running a household, or several. A home is a place with its own address: its people, the facts the house needs you to know, the things kept there and what needs doing. People who log in get an account; people who do not — a toddler, a relative you only keep notes about — still get a record, and what travels with them reads the same in every home they belong to. Pre-loaded with three homes — two separated parents and a grandparent — and three children who belong to all of them, rotating week on and week off between the parents with a one-off day at the grandparent's. The youngest has no account at all. Member accounts use the password "demo".
meta.author: Alex Kirk

steps.code:
<?php
use Households\Access;
use Households\Storage;
use Households\Whereabouts;

require_once '/wordpress/wp-load.php';

if ( ! taxonomy_exists( 'household' ) || ! class_exists( '\\Households\\Storage' ) ) {
	return;
}

$admin = get_user_by( 'login', 'admin' );
$admin_id = $admin ? (int) $admin->ID : 1;
$storage = new Storage();

// Nothing below is dated by hand. The demo is unpacked on a day nobody knows
// in advance and has to read as if it had been kept all along, so every date
// in it is worked out from that day: the week it falls in, and the changeover
// at the end of that week.
$today = current_time( 'Y-m-d' );
$on = static function ( string $date, string $shift = '' ): string {
	$day = new DateTimeImmutable( $date, new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ) );
	return ( '' === $shift ? $day : $day->modify( $shift ) )->format( 'Y-m-d' );
};
$monday = $on( $today, 'monday this week' );

// The plugin does not make accounts; WordPress does, and a person is pointed
// at one afterwards. The demo needs people who can log in, so it makes them
// here — which is exactly what whoever runs a real site would do.
$account = static function ( string $name, string $email ): int {
	if ( get_user_by( 'email', $email ) ) {
		return (int) get_user_by( 'email', $email )->ID;
	}
	$user_id = wp_insert_user( [
		'display_name' => $name,
		'first_name'   => $name,
		'role'         => Storage::WP_ROLE,
		'user_email'   => $email,
		'user_login'   => strtolower( $name ),
		'user_pass'    => 'demo',
	] );
	return is_wp_error( $user_id ) ? 0 : (int) $user_id;
};

// Three homes: two separated parents and a grandparent.
$home_a = $storage->create_home( "Sam's Home", $admin_id );
$home_b = $storage->create_home( "Jo's Home", $admin_id );
$home_c = $storage->create_home( "Nana's House", $admin_id );
if ( ! $home_a || ! $home_b || ! $home_c ) {
	return;
}

// Sam is whoever is logged in, so the demo opens on a home you belong to.
$sam = $storage->add_person( $home_a, 'Sam', [
	'birthdate' => $on( $today, '-38 years +200 days' ),
] );
Access::assign_user( $sam, $admin_id );

$jo = $storage->add_person( $home_b, 'Jo', [
	'birthdate' => $on( $today, '-40 years +45 days' ),
] );
Access::assign_user( $jo, $account( 'Jo', 'jo@example.com' ) );

$nana = $storage->add_person( $home_c, 'Nana', [
	'label' => 'Grandparent',
] );
Access::assign_user( $nana, $account( 'Nana', 'nana@example.com' ) );

$mia = $storage->add_person( $home_a, 'Mia', [
	'is_child'  => true,
	'birthdate' => $on( $today, '-9 years +12 days' ),
] );
Access::assign_user( $mia, $account( 'Mia', 'mia@example.com' ) );

$ben = $storage->add_person( $home_a, 'Ben', [
	'is_child'  => true,
	'birthdate' => $on( $today, '-6 years +80 days' ),
] );
Access::assign_user( $ben, $account( 'Ben', 'ben@example.com' ) );
// Pip has no account. Nobody logs in as a two-year-old, but her shoe size is
// still worth writing down, and both houses need to read the same answer.
$pip = $storage->add_person( $home_a, 'Pip', [
	'is_child'  => true,
	'birthdate' => $on( $today, '-2 years +150 days' ),
] );

// The children belong to all three homes; Sam can reach all three so the demo
// has something to show in the views that span homes. Belonging to a home is
// not the same as being at one, so where Sam is is said further down rather
// than guessed from three memberships.
foreach ( [ $mia, $ben, $pip ] as $child ) {
	Access::join( $child, $home_b );
	Access::join( $child, $home_c );
}
foreach ( [ $home_b, $home_c ] as $home ) {
	Access::join( $sam, $home );
}
foreach ( [ $home_a, $home_b, $home_c ] as $home ) {
	Access::set_admin( $home, $admin_id, true );
}
Access::set_admin( $home_b, Access::user_for_person( $jo ), true );
Access::set_admin( $home_c, Access::user_for_person( $nana ), true );

// Something written down in a house is only true if whoever it is for is in
// that house on the day it is due, so the two lists are dated by the stay
// rather than by a count of days: the children are at Sam's until Sunday and
// at Jo's the week after. A stay already half over cannot hold a day that has
// gone, so this week's dates come no earlier than today; next week's are
// whole and stand as they are.
$at_sams = static function ( int $weekday ) use ( $today, $monday, $on ): string {
	$date = $on( $monday, '+' . $weekday . ' days' );
	return $date < $today ? $today : $date;
};
$at_jos = static function ( int $weekday ) use ( $monday, $on ): string {
	return $on( $monday, '+' . ( 7 + $weekday ) . ' days' );
};

$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Pack school bag', $mia, 'task', $at_sams( 0 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Feed the cat', $ben, 'task', $at_sams( 0 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Dentist appointment', $ben, 'appointment', $at_sams( 1 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Swimming lesson', $mia, 'appointment', $at_sams( 2 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Parent-teacher meeting', $sam, 'appointment', $at_sams( 4 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Tidy room', $mia, 'task', $at_sams( 5 ) );

$storage->add_task( $home_b, 'Water the plants', $ben, 'task', $at_jos( 0 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_b, 'Practice piano', $mia, 'task', $at_jos( 1 ) );
$storage->add_task( $home_b, 'Renew passports', $jo, 'task', $at_jos( 6 ) );

// Nobody has to be anywhere for this one: it is the household's, not a
// person's, so the only thing its date has to be is far enough off to sit at
// the bottom of the fortnight.
$storage->add_task( $home_a, 'Book summer camp', 0, 'task', $at_jos( 3 ) );

// A size is a field, and the rest of what travels with a person is prose.
$storage->save_person( $mia, [
	'sizes' => [ 'clothing' => '134', 'shoe' => '33' ],
	'about' => "Allergic to peanuts and house dust.\nSwimming on Wednesdays, needs the blue bag.",
] );
$storage->save_person( $ben, [
	'sizes' => [ 'clothing' => '116', 'shoe' => '29' ],
	'about' => "Inhaler is in the kitchen drawer, both houses.",
] );
$storage->save_person( $pip, [
	'sizes' => [ 'clothing' => '92', 'shoe' => '22' ],
	'about' => "Still in nappies at night. Sleeps with the grey rabbit — it lives at whichever house she is at.",
] );

// Nobody types the date beside a size: it is stamped when the value changes,
// which in a demo built this morning would make every size look measured this
// morning. So the youngest one's is put back a few months by hand, because a
// size is only an answer if you can see how old it is — which is the whole
// argument for the field, and it does not show if they are all fresh.
update_post_meta( $pip, Storage::META_SIZES, [
	'clothing' => [ 'value' => '92', 'noted' => $on( $today, '-5 months' ) ],
	'shoe'     => [ 'value' => '22', 'noted' => $on( $today, '-5 months' ) ],
] );

// The things people ask about a house they are not in every day.
$storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::FACT, 'Wifi', 'Network "sams-wifi", password on the fridge door' );
$storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::FACT, 'Water main valve', 'Under the stairs, behind the coats' );
$storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::FACT, 'Bin day', 'Paper on Tuesday, everything else on Friday' );
$storage->add_note( $home_b, Storage::FACT, 'Wifi', 'Network "jos-flat", password taped under the router' );
$storage->add_note( $home_b, Storage::FACT, 'Spare key', 'With the neighbour in flat 3' );
$storage->add_note( $home_c, Storage::FACT, 'Wifi', 'Network "nana", ask Nana' );
$storage->add_note( $home_c, Storage::FACT, 'Doctor', 'Practice on the square, closed Wednesday afternoons' );

// A thing can be kept at more than one house, and is somewhere different in each.
$rabbit = $storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, 'Grey rabbit', 'Wherever Pip left it, usually her bed' );
$storage->keep_note_at( $home_b, Storage::ITEM, $rabbit, 'The sofa, or under it' );
$storage->keep_note_at( $home_c, Storage::ITEM, $rabbit, 'Toy box in the back bedroom' );
$booster = $storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, 'Booster seat', 'Hall cupboard, top shelf' );
$swimming = $storage->add_note( $home_b, Storage::ITEM, 'Swimming kit', 'Blue bag by the door on Wednesdays' );
$storage->add_note( $home_c, Storage::ITEM, 'Travel cot', 'Attic, with the spare bedding' );
$boots = $storage->add_note( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, 'Football boots', 'Shoe rack by the back door' );

// Where a thing lives and where it is are two questions. The rabbit lives at
// all three houses and is at Jo's this week. The booster seat lives at Sam's
// and has gone to Nana's, which does not keep it: lent rather than moved, so
// the hall cupboard is still where it lives and still says so.
$storage->say_note_is_at( $home_b, Storage::ITEM, $rabbit );
$storage->say_note_is_at( $home_c, Storage::ITEM, $booster );

// And where a thing is to get to is a third. The swimming kit has to be at
// Sam's for the lesson and is still at Jo's; the booster seat has to come back
// from Nana's; the football boots are on the shoe rack at Sam's and have to
// leave with the children on Monday, which is the ordinary case — a thing on
// the shelf you are standing at, wanted at the house you are going to. Saying
// so moves none of them: they are where they are until somebody carries them,
// and until then they are on the packlist.
$storage->say_note_goes_to( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, $swimming );
$storage->say_note_goes_to( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, $booster );
$storage->say_note_goes_to( $home_b, Storage::ITEM, $boots );

// And one of them is already in the bag by the door, which is not the same as
// having gone: it is at Jo's until somebody says the bag has been carried.
$storage->toggle_packed( $home_a, Storage::ITEM, $swimming );

// The children rotate week on, week off between the two parents' homes. Nana's
// is in the rotation as a third home, used for a single day the pattern knows
// nothing about.
foreach ( [ $mia, $ben, $pip ] as $child ) {
	Whereabouts::save_rotation( $child, [
		'pattern'         => Whereabouts::PATTERN_WEEK,
		'start_date'      => $monday,
		'homes'           => [ $home_a, $home_b, $home_c ],
		'changeover_time' => '17:00',
	] );
	Whereabouts::set_override( $child, $on( $monday, '+9 days' ), $home_c );
}

// Sam does not rotate: Sam lives at Sam's Home, and the children come and go
// around that. Three memberships cannot say which of them Sam is standing in,
// so the demo says it once, on the day before the week began. A statement with
// no pattern behind it still stands the day after it is made, which is how
// somebody who simply lives somewhere is written down — and it is what puts a
// household under today, so the index has a list to read.
Whereabouts::set_override( $sam, $on( $monday, '-1 day' ), $home_a );
